messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: reparameterized multi_normal + auto-dif var bloat
parts:
1. If the covariance matrix is constant data,
we can just invert it once and call

multi_normal_log(y,mu,Sigma); // Sigma covariance matrix
multi_normal_prec_log(y,mu,Tau); // Tau precision matrix

Then if the precision matrix Tau is data, the right
behavior falls out of the way we're dealing with
constants versus variables -- that is, we drop
the log(det(Tau)) term.

2. Another inefficiency comes from duplication in
values for symmetric matrices. It'd be better if
we could take only half a matrix, then use a
self-adjoint view of it (in Eigen's terminology) if we
need to treat it as a full matrix. The loop would
then simplify to

for (m in 1:K)
for (n in m:K)
...

We only need to do half (plus K/2) of the assigns.

A big obstacle is the poor interaction of Eigen template
expressions like self-adjoint and our auto-dif. That could
potentially be addressed, though I'm not exactly sure how
at the moment.

All of this is of course do-able in Stan[C++],
which doesn't have any training wheels. We can
turn off error checking altogether by configuring
the error policy (at least I think we can -- Daniel?)

- Bob

This relates to another issue I was wondering about. Why don't we have
an Eigen class called covarianceMatrix or whatever that inherits from
Matrix? The constructors for covarianceMatrix should guarantee
positive definiteness and then we can define density functions for
elliptical distributions that take a covarianceMatrix for Sigma where
we can take shortcuts and density functions that take a plain Matrix
where we have to do very thorough checking every iteration.

Ben

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] reparameterized multi_normal + auto-dif var bloat
parts:
In Boost's policies, there is an ignore_policy, so we could go ahead
and ignore error checking.

As of right now, the conditions are checked regardless of the policy.
This is Boost's default checking mechanism. When there is an error, a
method is called with the policy that has the right behavior. With
that said, I think we should ignore the error checking when the policy
is ignore_policy. There is a little subtlety in implementation. I
think we'll be alright once we push the policies through all of our
functions. Until then, we are dependent on the functions we call.
Hopefully none of them throw exceptions.

In short, we can turn off error checking. We need to reimplement our
error checking, but it can be done. I am in the process of revisiting
our error checking now anyway, so I'll start incorporating the
changes.

Great -- I thought there was something like "ignore_policy".

My thinking is that we could allow error policy to
be configured in the command call for the Stan GM.

I think we should default to doing enough checking to
catch errors on a per-sample basis.

As Daniel says, it'll take a while to push this through
all of our functions. There's probably nearly 100 of them,
so it's lots of work, and may not get done before v1.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: reparameterized multi_normal + auto-dif var bloat
parts:
There's not even a symmetrix-matrix Eigen class,
much less a positive-definite one.

You can take a regular matrix and provide a
symmetric (aka self-adjoint) view of it, but
this isn't the same -- it still takes M x N
storage, for instance.

Doug Bates has been really active lately on the
Eigen mailing list. Eventually, I'd like to help
Eigen by adding some of these things and also
by pushing through binary matrix ops of mixed
types (the same way they already do for complex).
There are pretty clear guidelines on how to do this
and their developers are very helpful on their
mailing lists, so I think it's doable. One of
the subtleties would be making it all work with
non-Dynamic matrices. The alignment seems to give
them lots of problems.

- Bob
